claims.text: Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 initially forms a high-temperature, single-phase BCC state.
Phase stability in Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 is primarily governed by competition between thermodynamic instability and kinetic limitations on atomic diffusion.
Al-induced chemical-potential differences provide a thermodynamic driving force for instability and phase separation.
Al atoms are relatively immobile in the high-temperature BCC state.
Limited Al mobility prevents rapid compositional partitioning.
Suppression of compositional partitioning kinetically preserves BCC even when BCC is thermodynamically metastable.
High configurational entropy contributes to maintenance of the high-temperature BCC state.
Kinetic barriers limit Al diffusion in the BCC state.
Slow cooling provides sufficient time for greater Al diffusion and partitioning than rapid quenching.
Al partitioning and local compositional fluctuations destabilize the BCC structure.
Local BCC destabilization promotes nucleation and growth of secondary phases.
Rapid quenching from the high-temperature state will preserve the BCC phase.
Slow cooling will produce secondary phases because it permits enhanced Al partitioning.
The secondary material formed during slow cooling may be an FCC phase or an intermetallic phase.
Rapidly quenched and slowly cooled samples will exhibit detectably different phase compositions and microstructures.
Substantial composition changes or additions of other elements may alter diffusion kinetics enough that the proposed mechanism no longer applies.
